Ran backend linter checks on modified Phase 2 files: no linter errors.

Stress test fix: added SQLite explicit-transaction queue/mutex in `ward-backend/db.js` and refactored transactional repos (`EscalationRepository`, `PatientRepository.discharge`) to use `withTransaction` to prevent nested-transaction crashes under concurrency.
Stress test fix: enabled WAL + `busy_timeout` in `ward-backend/db.js` to improve concurrent DB behavior for reads/writes.
Stress test fix: corrected `POST /api/patients/:patientId/medications/:medId/administer` insert placeholder count and added best-effort retry for SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED to prevent transient 500s.
Verification after stress-hardening: backend Jest still passes (11/11 suites; 26/26 tests).

Verification after meds/stress hardening: initial stress runner reported `server5xx: 0`. However, the runner’s DB seeding (while the backend was running) later caused `SQLITE_CORRUPT` during a subsequent Jest run. We restored the DB from git and confirmed Jest passes again.

Stress verification (safe mode): updated `ward-backend/stressEverything.js` to refuse DB seeding while `/health` is reachable; reran stress with seeding disabled (`CONCURRENCY=12`, `DURATION_SEC=18`) and confirmed `server5xx: 0`. Re-ran backend Jest (`npm test`) and confirmed all tests pass.

History endpoint fix: aligned `routes/history.js` with SQLite `DailyStats.type` CHECK constraints (persisted history under an allowed type) and added `tests/integration/history.test.js` to verify tenant scoping for history writes/reads; updated `withTransaction()` to recover after transactional failures.

Enterprise auth hardening: implemented DB-backed login lockouts (`AuthLoginAttempts`) keyed by username + client IP; updated `POST /api/auth/login` to enforce DB lockouts (429 on locked attempts) and reset on successful login; removed in-memory rate-limiter dependency for lockout enforcement. Updated `server.js` to set `trust proxy` so IP-based throttling/lockout works correctly behind reverse proxies. Tightened `middleware/auth.js` so missing `JWT_SECRET` fails in production. Verified via `ward-backend npm test` (auth rate limiting test still passes).
